newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thailand to raise natural, synthetic rubber output.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to raise natural, synthetic rubber output.

text.p: Thailand, the world's biggest natural rubber producer, plans to raise output to 1.9 million tonnes in 1997 and 2.0 million tonnes in 1998, officials of the Thai Rubber Association (TRA) said on Thursday.
V. Sinchareoknkul and W. Thainugul told an Asian Rubber Markets meeting most of the expansion in output would come from new rubber plantations in northeast Thailand.
"It is expected that Thai rubber production will reach 2.0 million tonnes in 1998," they said in a report, which added that output should rise to more than 1.9 million tonnes next year.

"This (northeast) region has great potential for rubber production with at least 1.6 million hectares which is suitable for rubber cultivation and income from rubber is higher than that of some upland crops presently grown in the region," they said.
One factor spurring the growth of Thai rubber production was the presence of many large car companies in the country. They include General Motors, Mitsubishi Motors and Toyota.
"The demand for natural tyre production is increasing. Many tyre factories are planning to expand their production capacity to meet the increasing requirements of the future," the TRA officials said.
Thailand is also gearing up to expand production of synthetic rubber production.

Three companies will begin operations in 1997 to produce 60,000 tonnes of synthetic rubber. Output is expected to rise to 160,000 tonnes in 1998. The factories are located in the Mabtaput industrial estate in Rayong province.
